newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk 1996 group pre-tax profit plunges.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk 1996 group pre-tax profit plunges.

text.p: NOTES -- Full company name is RAO Norilsky Nickel.
Figures prepared to Russian standards on an cash basis.
Production of nickel fell 1.6 percent in 1996 in comparison to 1995 production, according to the yearly report released at the annual shareholders meeting on Friday.
The report said copper production rose 0.4 percent and cobalt production fell 9.2 percent.
It also said platinum group metals production at the flagship metals combine, the Norilsky Gorno-Metallurgichesky Kombinat, rose by 3.5 percent in 1996 but fell by 26.7 percent at AO Severonikel.

Uneximbank controls a 38 percent stake in the group which is ultimately owned by the government. Other shareholders include Credit Suisse Moscow (4.5 percent), First Boston (4.7 percent), Bank of Bermuda (3.2 percent), Chase Manhattan (1.4 percent) and Pictet & CIE, Geneva (1.2 percent).

Russian accounting standards differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
